sentences.text: Smt . Aswathy S., IAS, Commissioner -cum-Secretary, Department of Health & Family Welfare Department, Govt. of Odisha has filed an affidavit dated 10.09.2025, wherein it is stated that the facility for online registration for OPD appointments under the Health and Family Welfare Department is available 24 hours for most of the District Headquarter Hospitals (DHH) and major Medical Colleges and Hospitals which includes SCBMCH, Cuttack, Acharya Harihar Cancer Institute, Cuttack and SVPPGIP, Cuttack.

entities.text: Department of Health & Family Welfare Department
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: It is further stated that the patients need to click on "Online Registration" and either enter their existing Central Registration Number (CR Number/OPD Ticket) or select "New Registration" for first-time registration.
They must then select the hospital, department, and appointment date, and fill in details such as name, age, and address.
Upon submission, the system generates a QR code along with an appointment slip that can either be printed directly or collected from the kiosk machine at Hospitals by scanning the QR code.
On the scheduled date, patients are required to visit the respective department with the appointment slip at least one hour before OPD closing time.
For subsequent visits, re-registration is mandatory using the previous CR Number to obtain a fresh appointment slip.
The names of the Doctors who would be in-charge of the OPD on a particular day is being displayed on the registration site.
The detailed procedure has been enclosed to the affidavit as Annexure-A.

entities.text: MAINTENANCE OF HYGIENIC  CONDITION OF CENTRAL KITCHEN
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: This issue was taken up on 11.07.2025.

On 11.09.2025 that day, we perused the report of the learned Advocates' Committee dated 19.06.2025, which indicated that in the Central Kitchen of SCBMCH, Cuttack, food is not being prepared in a hygienic manner, which was endangering the wellbeing of the patients.
Photographs of preparation of rotis manually for the patients were also being presented with a report.
On 11.07.2025, we also considered the affidavit dated 29.07.2025 of Prof. (Dr.) Goutam Kumar Satapathy, Superintendent I/c., SCBMCH, Cuttack.

The video clipping of the Central Kitchen of SCBMCH, Cuttack was also displayed in open Court on that day and we found that the persons who were preparing rotis were not using gloves, most of them had not covered their hairs and mouth and people wearing shoes were also allowed to enter inside the Central Kitchen.
On 11.07.2025, Prof. Satapathy assured this Court that he would look into all these aspects and ensure that proper hygienic condition is maintained in the process of making rotis.

Today, learned counsel for the State has produced the letter no.21501 dated 11.09.2025 of the Medical Superintendent, SCBMCH, Cuttack addressed to the learned Advocate General, wherein it is stated as follows:
(i) In order to maintain hygienic condition during the preparation of diet, the outsourcing agency M/s. Utkal Suppliers was instructed vide office letter No.17849 dated 31.07.2025 that all staff should use mask, gloves and caps while preparing diet in the kitchen.

entities.text: Registrar (Judicial) vs State Of Odisha & Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: (ii) Adhering to the instruction, proper hygiene is being maintained in the kitchen.
Rotis are being prepared using Roti Making machine.
The personnel engaged in preparation of cooking are using apron, gloves, mask, caps etc in the kitchen.
The kitchen work is being monitored by Dietician, and Hospital Managers on regular basis.
The letter dated 11.09.2025 of the Medical Superintendent, SCBMCH, Cuttack is taken on record.
Prof. (Dr.) Goutam Kumar Satapathy, Superintendent I/c., SCBMCH, Cuttack also sent a recording of the Central Kitchen which was displayed in open Court.

Regarding the works to be undertaken by the R & B Development, Prof. (Dr.) Goutam Kumar Satapathy, Superintendent I/c., SCBMCH, Cuttack submits that the electrical and civil works have been completed in the meantime.

Ministry of Health & Family Welfare, Govt. of India, in order to support the States to streamline and standardize the dietary service in the public hospitals, has prepared technical and operational guidelines in the year 2022 which is styled as "Guidelines for Modern Kitchen and Dietary Services"
with a vision to provide ergonomically designed, well-equipped modern kitchen so that clean,
hygienic and balanced diet can be delivered to the patients visiting the hospitals which would contribute patients' satisfaction.

entities.text: Ministry of Health & Family Welfare, Govt. of India
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Maintaining good nutrition during hospitalization is vital and it would prevent increased risk of hospital acquired infections, delayed wound healing, longer hospital stay, higher mortality and morbidity.

The Health Secretary, Govt. of Odisha shall constitute a team to study the aforesaid 2022 Guidelines and suggest as to how in the SCBMCH, Cuttack as well as other Govt. hospitals in Cuttack City, a well-planned infrastructure can be provided, infection preventive measures can be taken, protocols and process for preparation and distribution of cooked diet in a systematic way simultaneously ensuring quality can be maintained and submit a report in that respect.
Since the kitchen facility available in SCBMCH, Cuttack has been outsourced to M/s.
Utkal Suppliers, overall monitoring and supervision is required to be done by hospital personnel.
Since different dietary norms are to be followed for different category of patients, the role of dietician is very much relevant.
There should be adequacy of diet and hygienic measures are required to be taken at the time of food preparation and also while serving the food to the patients.

Department of Health & Family Welfare, Govt. of Odisha taking into account the continuing concern over the lack of attention to the nutritional needs of indoor patients, commissioned a technical and management support team to assess the prevailing dietary practices in public health institutions and to identify areas of improvement.

NEWS ITEMS PUBLISHED IN DAILY NEWSPAPER RELATING TO AIR POLLUTION IN CUTTACK CITY 320.

A news item published on 10.10.2025 in 11.09.2025 the vernacular daily "The Samaja" under the heading of "NIYANTRANA BAHARE PRADUSANA - ABETHU DHULI DHUANARE ANANISHWASI"
(Pollution out of control, an unbreathable condition due to dust and smoke) is brought to the notice of this Court.

entities.text: NIYANTRANA BAHARE PRADUSANA - ABETHU DHULI DHUANARE ANANISHWASI
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: It is stated that even though the rainy season is not over yet, but commuters on the road have started using clothes and masks on their faces.
As the sun rises, the streets of the city get covered with dust and smoke.
The situation gets deteriorated in the evening.
With the arrival of winter, there is every risk of increase in pollution level.
The Municipal Corporation and the District Administration are not paying any attention to this issue.
It is stated that the Pollution Control Board in Cuttack is currently in coma.
Clean air is essential for a healthy life.
It is also the right of everyone.
Therefore, every citizen, including the Government, has the responsibility and duty to ensure that it is clean.
Usually, air pollution is high during winter due to lack of humidity, but now, with the rainy season underway, the pollution level in Cuttack city is on rise.
After 11 a.m., the roads and the sky are covered with dust and smoke.
It is also seen that from afternoon till evening, the air is filled with dust.
The pollution level of the vehicles is not being checked.
Similarly, even though dust is piled up on the roads, it is not cleaned regularly.

While the CMC has a special Registrar (Judicial) vs State Of Odisha & Others .... Opp. ... on 11 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/18059576/
7 machine to clean the city's streets, it is not being used properly.

entities.text: Registrar (Judicial) vs State Of Odisha & Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: When a heap of garbage piles up at the city's riverbanks and piers, many times it is seen that it is being set on fire.
Especially in the evening, its smoke is making people uncomfortable.
Pollution control rules are not being followed at all in the Jagatpur area on the outskirts of the city.
Waste is dumped on the banks of the river.
Even materials containing various harmful chemical are being set on fire.
The smoke emitted from this is deadly for human beings and animals.
Although pollution is increasing year after year, the Administration and the Pollution Board have remained silent.
People in the Jagatpur area have raised their voice against the pollution.
As the festivals begin, lakhs of people will gather in Cuttack during Dusshera.
In such a situation, there is a possibility of further increase in pollution.
Therefore, the CMC and the District Administration need to take proactive steps in this direction.
The news item is taken on record.

Ms. Rashmita Priyadarshini, Regional Officer, Odisha State Pollution Control Board,
Cuttack has to play a key role in this issue, is present.

The traffic management in and around the temple forms an integral part in ensuring that the devotees, who are expected to throng the temple, do not face any inconvenience.
